prompt: Streaming platforms have largely replaced scheduled television and, for many people, trips to the cinema. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this change.
essay:
Watching at a time of one's own choosing has replaced watching at a time chosen by a broadcaster, and cinema attendance has fallen accordingly. The change has clear benefits for viewers, but its effects on what actually gets made are less comfortable.

The advantages for the audience are substantial and easy to state. Control over timing is the obvious one, and it matters most to the people whose hours are least predictable — shift workers, parents of small children, anyone for whom a fixed nine o'clock broadcast was simply unavailable. Beyond convenience, the range of material has widened enormously: series in other languages now reach audiences that a national broadcaster would never have commissioned them for, and older work that would once have vanished remains permanently available. Price is a further advantage for households that watch a great deal, though the proliferation of competing services has eroded it.

The disadvantages are less visible because they operate on production rather than on viewing. Platforms commission according to what their data suggests will retain subscribers, which favours material that resembles material that has already worked. The economics of cinema are affected too: a film that needs a large screen and a long run to find its audience is harder to finance when the default destination is a living room. Something is also lost socially — a broadcast watched by millions at once created a shared reference that a personalised library does not.

Overall the gains to viewers are real, and I would not want the schedule back. But it is worth being clear that convenience has been paid for in a currency the viewer never sees: a narrower range of things commissioned, and fewer occasions on which a whole country watches the same thing.
title: Streaming instead of schedules and cinemas
